newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes up slightly against US dollar.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes up slightly against US dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed up slightly at 8.2966 against the U.S. dollar on Friday from Thursday's 8.2967, with no reaction seen to the announcement of China's increased foreign exchange reserves, traders said.
China's foreign reserves hit $105 billion at the end of 1996, up from $73.5 billion at the end of 1995, Xinhua news agency quoted Vice Premier Zhu Rongji as telling a meeting in Beijing.
Dealers said that the increase, which had been expected in the market, had no direct influence on the yuan's trend and that today's price movements were stable.
The yuan opened unchanged at 8.2967 and consolidated around 8.2966 for the whole session, hitting an intra-day high of 8.2964 and a low of 8.2970.
Trading was extremely dull, with most done at 8.2966, traders said.
"The yuan's upward trend continued, although slowly, due to large demand for the local unit ahead of the Chinese lunar new year," one dealer said.
"Trading is usually dull ahead of the weekend, which also limited the yuan's movement," a second dealer said.
Dealers expect the yuan to consolidate up further early next week.
The yuan closed down at 7.1450 from 7.1410 against 100 Japanese yen and up at 1.0727 from 1.0734 against the Hong Kong dollar.
